eventops.title: EventOps
eventops.summary: Calendar, staff and finances for your events company.
eventops.metaDescription: EventOps brings the calendar, clients, staff and finances of an event company into a single system. A ShippersLab own product, in production.
eventops.lead: The calendar, clients, staff and finances of your events company in one place. It is a ShippersLab own product, in production and used every day by events companies.

sections.title: Why we built it.
body: Events companies coordinate dates, staff and payments with spreadsheets and messages. We saw that does not scale and built a system around the way they work.
We offer it as our own product, so any events company can get organized without commissioning custom software.

sections.title: The problem.
body: An events company juggles dates, crews, clients and payments at once. With everything spread across spreadsheets and messages, two events overlap, staff is missing and nobody knows how much came in and how much is still owed.
If you still run it on spreadsheets, read [how to organize an events company](/blog/como-organizar-una-empresa-de-eventos).

sections.title: What we built.
body: EventOps puts the whole operation in one system. Each event has its client, its team and its money, and the calendar shows at a glance what to do and when.
The whole team always sees the same information, with nothing to copy from one spreadsheet to another.

sections.title: How we built it.
body: We designed and developed it ourselves, from the interface to the full system. Each company signs in with its own users, invited by email, and sees only its own data.
We talk to the people using it often and every improvement comes from what they need day to day.

sections.title: How it works.
body: You create an event once, with its client and dates: site visit, setup, sound check and teardown. Then you build the quote, which goes out as a PDF with your logo, and assign staff while seeing who is free. There is a [free quote template](https://eventops.digital/plantilla-presupuesto-eventos) and a guide to [staff payment and assignment](https://eventops.digital/gestion-de-personal).
To get paid, you record the deposit and installments in pesos or dollars, along with expenses. The monthly summary shows what came in and what is still owed, and everything exports to CSV.

sections.title: Where it stands.
body: EventOps is in production and events companies use it.

eventops.productTitle: Get your events company in order.
eventops.productDescription: Calendar, clients, staff and finances in one system. Try it on your next event.

tuturnero.metaDescription: Tuturnero gives each business a page with a link and QR code so clients book without an account and without a commission. A ShippersLab own product.
galleryAlts: Three steps to create a Tuturnero page
A court booking page in Tuturnero
tuturnero.lead: A multi-industry booking tool. Create your account, set up your booking page and start receiving appointments. It is built for courts, clinics, salons and any business that works by appointment. It is an own product and real customers already use it.

sections.title: Why we built it.
body: A business that works by appointment (a court, a clinic, a salon) usually books over messages. We thought booking an appointment should not take a conversation.
We wanted something that works for any industry, sets up in minutes and does not make anyone install or learn anything.

sections.title: The problem.
body: Every appointment is an exchange: the client asks what is free, someone checks the schedule, replies, confirms and writes it down. If two people ask for the same time, one of them is left without a slot.
For the business it is lost time. For the client it is waiting on a reply for something that should take a minute.

sections.title: What we built.
body: Tuturnero gives each business a booking page with its brand, its hours and a short link with a QR code. The client picks a free time, leaves a name and books, without creating an account.
The business receives each request and accepts or declines it with one tap. What it confirms is taken on the schedule, so nobody else can book that time.

sections.title: How we built it.
body: We designed and built it ourselves, from the interface to the code. We made it usable without explanations: you sign in with Google, set when you are open and your page is ready.
Each business sets its own hours, holidays and vacations, and the system prevents double bookings on its own. What we add comes from what the people already using it tell us.

sections.title: How it works.
body: You create your account, upload your banner and photo, and set the days and hours you are open. Then you share the link on Instagram, over WhatsApp or with the QR code at the counter.
Do people book by phone? You can add those by hand too.

sections.title: Where it stands.
body: Tuturnero is in production. Customers already use it every day and we work with them to improve it.
Creating your page is free on the Inicial plan and bookings have no commission.

tuturnero.productDescription: Create a free account, set your hours and share your link. You are up and running in minutes.

estacionar.title: Estacionar
estacionar.summary: The identity of a marketplace to rent and find parking spaces.
estacionar.metaDescription: Estacionar connects people with an unused garage to drivers looking for parking. A ShippersLab own product: brand, app and landing page. Not published yet.
estacionar.lead: A marketplace to rent out the garage you do not use or find parking in any city, even on vacation. Our idea, designed and built by us.

images.alt: Estacionar logo on a yellow background
Estacionar logo and wordmark on a dark grid

sections.title: Why we built it.
body: There are empty garages and people circling without finding a place to park. Both sides exist in the same city and almost never meet.
The idea was ours: something like Airbnb for parking. We took it on as our own product and took it seriously.

sections.title: The problem.
body: Anyone with an unused garage or space has no simple place to rent it out. Anyone driving does not know where there is room and loses time looking.
And on vacation in another city, figuring out where to leave the car becomes one more problem.

sections.title: What we built.
body: A marketplace with three sides on one platform. Drivers search for parking by city and book the spot. Garage owners list a space they do not use and rent it out.
Commercial parking lots could join too: our plan was to talk to parking lots in different cities so they could load their profile and prices.

sections.title: How we built it.
body: We did it end to end ourselves: the brand, the social media, a web app and a landing page.

We thought of the colors in terms of traffic: road signs, roads and garages. That is why we chose yellow and black, a palette you can see from far away. The logo is a P for parking combined with a map pin.

sections.title: Where it stands.
body: Estacionar is not published yet. The brand is defined, the social media is set up, and the web app and the landing page are built.
We keep thinking of it as our own product.

examples.title: What it looks like in different businesses.

items.title: Distributor or wholesaler
items.body: Orders come in over WhatsApp, inventory lives in an Excel file and nobody's quite sure what's in the warehouse. An inventory and sales system can update stock when an order is confirmed and show you what to restock before you run out.

items.title: Appointment-based business
items.body: In a clinic, a repair shop or a beauty salon, the schedule often lives in a notebook or on one person's phone. A booking system brings together the team's calendar, each client's history and the day's payments.

items.title: Event company
items.body: Dates, crew and payments spread across chats and spreadsheets. That's what EventOps solves: a calendar with site visits, setup and teardown, clients with their history, crew assigned per date and each month's results.

process.title: How we work and how we quote.

steps.title: A 30-minute call
steps.body: What gets entered, who enters it and where things get stuck. That tells us where to start.

steps.title: A scope document
steps.body: What's in, what's out, what it costs and when it'll be ready. All clear before we start.

steps.title: Partial deliveries every week
steps.body: If the system is large, we split it up and start with what hurts most, like inventory or orders. Every week you see a working piece and try it with your team.

steps.title: Rollout
steps.body: We roll it out with your team and adjust it based on real use.

pricing.label: Price and timeline
pricing.body: They depend on how many parts the system has and what it needs to connect to. If you already pay for hosting or other services, we use them. If not, we handle them and charge their cost plus a management fee.

afterDelivery.label: Warranty
afterDelivery.body: If a bug turns up on our side, we fix it under warranty.

afterDelivery.label: Maintenance
afterDelivery.body: Optional, for changes and improvements after launch. Without it, the project costs less.

afterDelivery.label: Your data
afterDelivery.body: It's confidential and we only use it for your project.

items.question: Should I get a custom system or an off-the-shelf one?
items.answer: If an off-the-shelf system fits how you work, it may be enough. A custom system makes sense when your operation has its own steps that packaged software doesn't cover, or when you end up using three programs and a spreadsheet to fill the gaps. In the first conversation we tell you what we think fits your case.

items.question: I run everything on Excel today. What happens to that data?
items.answer: We start from there. We move your product, client or order spreadsheets into the new system, and that's planned in the proposal. If a spreadsheet still works for you, we can keep it connected.

items.question: Will my team be able to use it?
items.answer: We build it around how your team works, and they test it every week while it's being built. If you want, we add a training session so everyone can use it from day one.

items.question: Who owns the system, and what happens to my data?
items.answer: Your data is confidential and we only use it for your project. Who owns the code depends on whether it's a custom build or one of our products like EventOps. We put it in writing in the proposal before we start.

faq.title: Questions about websites, booking pages and catalogs.

items.question: Can I update prices and products myself?
items.answer: We can add a dashboard so you can edit prices, photos and products without depending on anyone. We define it in the proposal based on how often your catalog changes.

items.question: How is this different from opening a store on an e-commerce platform?
items.answer: E-commerce platforms make sense if you want checkout with a cart and automated shipping. If your customers already buy from you on WhatsApp, a catalog with WhatsApp ordering is usually simpler: they pick, message you with the order ready, and you keep selling the way you always have. We help you figure out which one fits.

items.question: Can the booking page send reminders?
items.answer: It can be included. Reminders, cancellations and rescheduling are defined in the proposal based on what your business needs.

items.question: Will the site show up on Google?
items.answer: We build it so Google can read it properly: every page with its own title, description and content, and fast on mobile. Ranking high takes time and depends on how many people search for what you offer. We do not promise rankings.

items.question: I already have an old website. Do you rebuild it or fix it?
items.answer: It depends on how it was built. We take a look, and if improving it makes more sense than starting over, we say so in the proposal.

faq.title: Questions about bots and AI agents.

items.question: Does it work with my current WhatsApp number?
items.answer: It depends on how you use that number today. We assess each case and walk you through the options before we start.

items.question: What if the bot says something wrong?
items.answer: The bot answers with the information we give it: your prices, your hours, your catalog. If it does not know something, it says so and hands the conversation to you. You test it before your customers ever see it.

items.question: What is the difference between a bot and an AI agent?
items.answer: A bot follows a set path, with menus, options and fixed answers. An AI agent understands what the customer writes in their own words and can take actions, like checking your stock or booking an appointment. We use AI where it helps resolve the request, and a simple bot when that is enough.

items.question: Can I see the conversations and reply myself?
items.answer: It can be added depending on the project, for example an inbox to review what the bot said or a direct handoff to your WhatsApp. We define it in the proposal.

items.question: Does it replace my support team?
items.answer: It takes care of the repetitive questions so your team can focus on what needs a person: a complaint, a large sale, a special case.

covers.body: Data that moves by hand from one place to another: an order that comes in on WhatsApp and gets typed into a spreadsheet, a sale you collect in one place and invoice in another. We connect those pieces so the data is entered once and nobody has to copy it. If you sell online, we also do [Tiendanube development](/integraciones/tiendanube): migration from WooCommerce, wholesale prices and connected stock.

items.title: Mercado Pago: payments and reconciliation
items.body: Every payment that comes in through Mercado Pago can be recorded automatically in your spreadsheet or system, linked to its order. Reconciliation stops being a line-by-line review at the end of the month, and you see right away what is paid and what is pending.

items.title: Tiendanube: stock and orders
items.body: If you sell online and in a physical shop, there should be a single stock. We sync Tiendanube inventory with your spreadsheet or system and make each new order reach whoever prepares it, without checking the dashboard. To set up the store, migrate from WooCommerce or configure wholesale prices, the detail is in [Tiendanube development and integration](/integraciones/tiendanube). If the wholesaler or distributor order is the center and the store is one more channel, that circuit is the [order management system](/sistemas-de-gestion/pedidos).

items.title: ARCA electronic invoicing
items.body: We connect your sales to ARCA (formerly AFIP) electronic invoicing services so the invoice is issued automatically when a payment or order is confirmed. You set the rules: which receipt type, for whom and when.

items.title: AI WhatsApp bot
items.body: A WhatsApp assistant that answers common questions, takes orders or bookings and records them where they belong. When a conversation needs a person, it hands it over. We build it with your answers and your rules, not generic scripts. If that order has to reserve stock and reach the invoice, we record it in an [order management system](/sistemas-de-gestion/pedidos).

items.title: Google Sheets and CRM
items.body: If your team works in Google Sheets or a CRM, we use it as the hub: orders, payments and contacts from other tools arrive there organized, and changes you make there are reflected wherever needed.

process.title: How we work and how we quote.

steps.title: A 30-minute call
steps.body: We look at how data moves today: where it comes in, where it gets copied by hand and where it gets lost. That shows which connection saves you the most work.

steps.title: A scope document
steps.body: What gets connected, what happens if something fails and what we need from you. Price and timeline in writing before we start.

steps.title: Partial deliveries every week
steps.body: We connect each tool through its official API, and every week you test a working piece with your real cases.

steps.title: Rollout
steps.body: We leave it running with your team. Every integration alerts you when something does not go as expected.

pricing.label: Price and timeline
pricing.body: We charge an implementation fee based on the complexity of the integration and, once it is running, a maintenance fee. Some tools charge for their own usage: if you already have the accounts, we use them; if not, we handle them and charge you their cost.

afterDelivery.label: Warranty
afterDelivery.body: If an integration fails because of a bug on our side, we fix it under warranty.

afterDelivery.label: Maintenance
afterDelivery.body: Covers the adjustments when an external tool changes how it connects. Without it, that adjustment is on you.

afterDelivery.label: Your data
afterDelivery.body: It's confidential and we only use it for your project.

items.question: Which tools can you connect?
items.answer: WhatsApp, Google Sheets, Mercado Pago, Tiendanube, ARCA electronic invoicing and CRMs, among other tools that offer a way to connect from outside (an API). If yours does not, we look at it in our first conversation and tell you the alternatives.

items.question: Can you connect ARCA (formerly AFIP) electronic invoicing?
items.answer: Yes. We connect your sales to ARCA so each invoice is issued without entering it by hand. In our first conversation we go over which account details are needed and help you set them up.

items.question: What happens if an integration breaks?
items.answer: We build every integration to alert you when something fails. If the bug is ours, we fix it. If an external tool you chose changes how it connects, the adjustment is on you, unless you have a maintenance plan with us.

items.question: Should I do this or build a new system?
items.answer: If what you use today works and the problem is moving data by hand, connecting is usually faster and cheaper. If your tools no longer give you what you need, a management system may make more sense. We tell you in the first conversation.

items.question: Can't I just do this myself with Zapier or Make?
items.answer: For simple connections, yes, and sometimes that is what we recommend. When there are rules specific to your business, many steps or high volume, it pays to have something custom built that you can control.

tiendanube.metaDescription: We build your Tiendanube store: migrate from WooCommerce, set up wholesale prices and connect stock to your management system. Scope and price in writing.
tiendanube.lead: We migrate the catalog from WooCommerce, set up wholesale and retail prices, and connect stock, invoicing and measurement. The domain stays yours.

covers.title: What we solve.
covers.body: A WooCommerce store that no longer holds up, wholesale orders put together by hand over WhatsApp, or stock entered in two places that never match. We sort it out on Tiendanube, with your domain and email left as they are. Scope and price in writing before we start.

items.title: Migrate WooCommerce to Tiendanube
items.body: Your whole catalog moves to Tiendanube: products, prices, SKUs, categories and images, with variants grouped by size or color. We move it with our own script, and order history stays in WooCommerce unless we add it to the scope. The step by step for keeping rankings is in [How to migrate from WooCommerce to Tiendanube](/blog/como-migrar-de-woocommerce-a-tiendanube).

items.title: Wholesale prices
items.body: Your wholesale buyers log in and see their price, with their own payment and shipping methods and a minimum order. We set it up with Tiendanube's native wholesale price list.

items.title: The store theme
items.body: Your store looks like your brand, with an adapted theme or a custom one. Tiendanube hosts the checkout and we don't redesign it.

items.title: Management system and invoicing
items.body: Stock and retail prices update on their own between the store and systems such as Tango or Contabilium. Each sale is invoiced with ARCA through an invoicing app connected to the store.

items.title: Measurement ready for ads
items.body: You reach your first campaign knowing which ad brings sales. We connect the Meta Pixel and Conversions API, Google Analytics 4 and Merchant Center, and check it all with a test purchase.

items.title: Domain, email and 301 redirects
items.body: Your domain stays where it is and email keeps arriving, because we leave its records alone. Every old URL redirects to the new one with a 301, so people coming from Google don't land on an error.

items.title: When a custom store makes more sense
items.body: If wholesale prices come from your system, or the checkout needs rules Tiendanube doesn't allow, a store of your own fits better. We build it as a [custom management system](/sistemas-de-gestion), plus hosting and maintenance.

audience.title: Who it's for.
audience.intro: For shops that already sell online, or want to start, and need the store to fit how they work: with wholesale buyers, with a stock system or with years of catalog in WooCommerce.

items.title: Shops on WooCommerce
items.body: The store grew and keeping it running became a job of its own.

items.title: Wholesalers and distributors
items.body: They want to sell online at their price without building every order over WhatsApp.

items.title: Shops already on Tiendanube
items.body: Stock lives in another system and gets entered twice.

process.title: How we work and how we quote.

steps.title: A 30-minute call
steps.body: We look at how you sell today: WooCommerce or another store, whether you have wholesale prices, which system holds stock and prices, and who manages the domain and email.

steps.title: A scope document
steps.body: What migrates, which Tiendanube plan you need, what gets connected and what stays out. Price and timeline in writing before we start.

steps.title: Partial deliveries every week
steps.body: We work on a test store. Every week you see a working piece: the loaded catalog, the theme, the wholesale list or the sync, and you try it with real products.

steps.title: Rollout
steps.body: We connect the domain without touching email, load the redirects and set up payment and shipping: Envío Nube, in-store pickup or rates by zone. We close with a test purchase to validate measurement.

pricing.body: They depend on catalog size, on how much variant and category cleanup is needed, on the theme and on whether a management system needs connecting. The Tiendanube plan and any paid apps are paid separately, directly to each provider. If email stays on your current hosting, that hosting keeps being billed.

afterDelivery.label: Warranty
afterDelivery.body: If a bug is on our side, we fix it under warranty.

afterDelivery.label: Maintenance
afterDelivery.body: Optional, for changes and for the adjustments when Tiendanube or a connected app changes how it connects. Without it, that adjustment is on you.

items.question: Can you migrate WooCommerce to Tiendanube?
items.answer: Yes. We move products, prices, SKUs, categories and images with our own script. Order history stays in WooCommerce unless we add it to the scope. Customer passwords don't carry over with this method, so each customer creates a new account.

items.question: Which Tiendanube plan do I need for wholesale prices?
items.answer: The native wholesale price list is available from the Impulso plan up. Tiendanube updates its plans, so the scope document tells you which one fits your store.

items.question: Can ARCA invoicing run automatically?
items.answer: Yes, with an invoicing app connected to the store. If you collect with Pago Nube, automatic invoicing currently works only with Facturante, and with other apps invoices are issued by hand.

items.question: Do you integrate Tiendanube with a management system?
items.answer: Yes, when the system has a way to connect. Stock and retail prices sync. Wholesale prices are loaded and kept in the store.

items.question: Do 301 redirects protect rankings in a migration?
items.answer: Yes. They send people coming from Google, or from an old link, to the new URL instead of an error. We map products, categories and pages, and the domain stays the same.

items.question: When is a custom store a better fit than Tiendanube?
items.answer: When wholesale prices have to come from the management system, or when the checkout needs rules Tiendanube doesn't allow. If the platform covers payments, shipping, wholesale and invoicing, Tiendanube is usually the shortest path.

pedidos.metaDescription: Wholesale orders, per-customer price lists and stock in one system for factories and distributors. Scope and price in writing.
pedidos.h1: Order management system for factories, distributors and wholesalers
pedidos.lead: Each order is entered once, from WhatsApp, a salesperson or the web, and preparation, stock and the invoice come out of it. Built around how you sell today.

covers.title: What we solve.
covers.body: The order arrives on WhatsApp, by email or on paper. Someone types it into Excel. The warehouse does not know what to pick until they are told, and the invoice is issued somewhere else, with the same data again. Along the way a case goes missing, an old price gets charged or stock is promised that is not there. An order management system joins that chain. We build it around how you sell today, and we can start with the stretch that eats the most time.

tools.title: What your order system can include.
tools.intro: You choose the modules. We start with the one that hurts most, usually order entry or stock, and the rest comes in once that stretch is in use. What follows can be included, and each module is chosen separately.

items.title: Order entry from any channel
items.body: An order can come in on WhatsApp, from a salesperson on the road, at the counter or through a web portal, and it stays the same order: customer, products and the price that customer gets. If taking orders on WhatsApp ends in a chat someone copies into a spreadsheet, that order can be left entered without the second pass. Entry from the phone, for the salesperson on the road, can be defined in the scope.

items.title: A price list per customer
items.body: Each customer can have their own list: wholesale, retail or a channel of their own, with a minimum order and a different price for a case or a single unit. When the order is entered, the price comes from that list. If the lists live in Excel, importing them can be included so nobody retypes them.

items.title: A status for every order
items.body: Each order moves through a status: received, being prepared, ready and delivered. Sales sees what came in, the warehouse sees what to pick and admin sees what still needs an invoice or a payment. Tracking shows where each one stands, and profiles are set by area.

items.title: Stock reserved on confirmation
items.body: On confirmation, that stock is reserved and stops being available for the next order. If you have more than one warehouse, stock can be kept separate and the order draws from the one that applies. Reorder alerts fire before the shortage reaches the customer. Orders and stock end up in one place.

items.title: Customer balance and collections
items.body: Each customer has a balance: what they ordered, what was invoiced and what they paid. A payment can be recorded on the road or when it comes in through Mercado Pago, and it is assigned to that customer.

items.title: From the order to production
items.body: In a factory that makes to order, confirming can open a production order with the promised date. For a factory, this piece starts from that production order.

tools.closing: Presales on the phone, route sheets, a portal where the customer builds their own order, and importing price lists from Excel can also be looked at for the scope. What goes in is written in the scope.

connections.title: Connected to what you already use.
connections.intro: What already works stays, and the system connects to it. Each piece, and the moment the data has to move, is in [integrations](/integraciones).

items.title: ARCA electronic invoicing
items.body: The invoice can be issued when the order is confirmed or when it is handed over. Invoicing uses the customer, the items and the price already on the order. You set the moment and the receipt type.

items.title: Mercado Pago
items.body: A payment that comes in through Mercado Pago can be assigned to the order and to the customer's account. Reconciliation stops being a match of a statement against a spreadsheet.

items.title: WhatsApp
items.body: A bot can take the order in the chat, on that customer's list, and leave it entered. If the conversation needs a person, it hands the chat over. The bot is built in [AI bots](/bots-con-ia). The order system receives the result.

items.title: Online store or B2B portal
items.body: Online sales can live on Tiendanube, on another platform or on a portal of your own. Tiendanube is one option when you already sell there or when its checkout is enough: building that store is in [Tiendanube development](/integraciones/tiendanube). If the price, the minimum or the assortment does not fit a packaged store, a portal of your own can be included as a [website or catalog](/webs-y-catalogos), tied to the same order.

audience.title: Who it's for.
audience.intro: It fits when the order is the center of the day and today it falls apart between the chat, the spreadsheet and the program where you invoice. It is shaped by who sells and how the goods leave.

items.title: Distributors with field sales and routes
items.body: The salesperson writes the order down and at night someone types it in. The warehouse picks late and the truck leaves with whatever was ready. An order system for a distributor can leave the order entered on the visit, with that customer's list. If you run a route every day, as a food or beverage distributor does, it can be built around that route.

items.title: Wholesalers with a counter and online sales
items.body: The counter sells at one price and the web at another, and stock finds out late. A system for wholesalers joins both channels, each with its own list. Counter and route use the same order, and the invoice can be issued when the order is picked up or when it is dispatched.

items.title: Factories that produce to order
items.body: There is a promised date and what has to be made to meet it. Confirming the order can open the production order. Tracking shows whether that date still holds.

flow.title: What an order looks like from end to end.
flow.intro: This path is an example circuit, so the pieces can be seen in order. Yours is written in the scope, based on how you work today.

steps.title: Entry
steps.body: The order comes in through the channel you use and lands with the customer, the products and the price from their list. If something is missing or the minimum is not met, that shows before it goes to be picked.

steps.title: Picking
steps.body: The warehouse sees what to pick. On confirmation, stock for those items is reserved. If there is not enough, the order shows it before promising a delivery date.

steps.title: Handover with an ARCA invoice
steps.body: When the goods leave, or on confirmation if you set it that way, the ARCA invoice is issued with the order data.

steps.title: Collection
steps.body: The payment is recorded against that order and the customer's balance updates. What is still unpaid stays visible, without rebuilding it at month end.

comparison.title: Custom, or a packaged system for distributors?
paragraphs: A packaged system for distributors is enough when your circuit fits what that program already does and the team can work that way, without a spreadsheet beside it. Custom is the better fit when the path is your own: several programs plus Excel, price, warehouse or route rules that cannot be configured, or when it has to connect to what you already have.

On the first call we tell you which of the two looks like the better fit. We do not publish a price: it depends on the modules, the permissions and the connections. How that number is worked out is in [what a custom management system costs](/blog/cuanto-cuesta-un-sistema-de-gestion-a-medida). If the order is one part of a larger operation, the wider frame is [management systems](/sistemas-de-gestion).

If you want to see a system that is built and in production, the [EventOps](/casos/eventops) case is our own product for event companies: each event is entered once, and the calendar, the quote and the payments come out of it. It shows how we build from each company's real operation.

items.question: Can orders come in on WhatsApp and be entered on their own?
items.answer: That can be included. A bot takes the order in the chat, with that customer's list, and leaves it entered. If the conversation leaves what the bot knows, it hands the chat to a person. If typing it in from the message is enough today, it can stay that way and the bot can be added later. It is defined in the scope.

items.question: Can I have a different price list for each customer?
items.answer: Yes. Each customer can have their own list, wholesale, retail or a channel of their own, with minimums and a price by case or by unit. When the order is entered, the price comes from that list. If the lists are in Excel today, importing them can be included.

items.question: Does the system invoice in ARCA when I confirm or hand over an order?
items.answer: That can be included. The ARCA e-invoice is issued at the moment you set: on confirmation or when the goods leave. It uses the data on the order, so the sale is not typed again. The receipt type is written in the scope.

items.question: Can my salespeople enter orders from a phone?
items.answer: Entering orders from a phone can go in the scope, with each customer's list. If your route has areas with no signal, we look at that on the call, based on your route.

items.question: Is a custom system a better fit, or one already built for distributors?
items.answer: If a system already built for distributors covers your circuit and the team can leave the spreadsheet, it can be enough. Custom is the better fit when there are steps of your own, when you use several programs plus Excel, or when it has to connect to what you already have. On the first call we tell you what looks like the better fit. The price comes from the scope, in writing.
